findings.evidence: grep for `charFun_star_kernel_posSemidef_of_star_eq_neg` in ./code returns only line 26 (docstring) and line 51 (declaration). `IsPositiveDefinite.posSemidef : IsPositiveDefinite F → Matrix.PosSemidef (fun a b => F (a + star b))` matches the statement verbatim with `F := charFun μ`.
findings.fix: Delete the theorem and its `## Main declarations` bullet (line 26); consumers wanting the kernel use `charFun_posSemidef`, and consumers wanting the `a + star b` form use `(charFun_isPositiveDefinite_of_star_eq_neg hstar).posSemidef`.
findings.issue: `charFun_star_kernel_posSemidef_of_star_eq_neg` carries `[StarAddMonoid E]` and `hstar : ∀ x, star x = -x` but states nothing beyond the generic corollary: it is literally `(charFun_isPositiveDefinite_of_star_eq_neg hstar).posSemidef` (same file, line 68 + `IsPositiveDefinite.posSemidef`, TauCeti/Analysis/PositiveDefinite/Basic.lean:185), and the hypothesis-free kernel statement it specializes was deleted in this PR. It has no in-repository user.

findings.evidence: `theorem charFun_posSemidef {ι : Type*} (t : ι → E) : (Matrix.of fun i j => charFun μ (t i - t j)).PosSemidef` (CharFun/PosDef.lean:124); call sites read `(charFun_posSemidef (μ := ν) (fun x : W => x)).submatrix (fun a : W => (-2 * Real.pi) • a)` (Convention.lean:121-122) and the analogous line at Gaussian/Basic.lean:123-124.
findings.fix: Call the general form directly — `charFun_posSemidef (μ := ν) (fun a : W => (-2 * Real.pi) • a)` and `charFun_posSemidef (μ := stdGaussian V) (fun a : V => Real.sqrt (2 * c) • a)` — and keep only the single equality rewrite to the target kernel.
findings.issue: `charFun_posSemidef {ι} (t : ι → E)` (TauCeti/Analysis/Bochner/CharFun/PosDef.lean:124) is already stated for an arbitrary family, but this proof takes the identity instance and then re-applies `.submatrix (fun a => (-2 * Real.pi) • a)`, re-deriving the pullback the lemma states directly; the detour is what forces the `Matrix.submatrix`/`Matrix.of` transport block that follows. Same pattern at TauCeti/Analysis/Bochner/Gaussian/Basic.lean:123 with `fun a : V => Real.sqrt (2 * c) • a`.

summary: The migration itself moves the API to the right level (Mathlib's `Matrix.PosSemidef`, arbitrary index type, no `Finite` restriction). Two leftovers sit below that level: a `star`-hypothesis kernel wrapper kept after its hypothesis-free sibling was deleted, and two call sites that instantiate the general `charFun_posSemidef` at the identity and then re-derive the pullback it already provides.
